DELIVER BY BOAT. FIND YOUR ROUTE.

Mangrove Express is a physics-driven delivery adventure set across the waterways of a tropical cyber world.

Take delivery jobs from local residents, load up your boat, and navigate through canals to find the right recipient. Steer through narrow passages, dodge hazards, manage your momentum, and when pulling over is not an option, toss the parcel straight to the customer.

Every delivery is a simple job—until it isn’t  :)

MASTER THE WATERWAYS

Your boat carries its momentum with it. You control the motor handle directly with your mouse, learning how to push, pull, turn, drift, and recover as the boat reacts to your movement.

Thread your way through obstacles, traffic, tight spaces, and unexpected situations. A clean route is easy to imagine—but much harder to keep under control.

CHART YOUR OWN ROUTE

Explore waterside communities and find your own way to each destination.

In Mangrove Express, the job is simple: pick up the package, find the customer, and make the delivery.

What happens between those steps is up to your hands.

Spin. Build. Reincarnate.

ManiWheel is an idle incremental game about combining letters and accumulating Virtue and Mercy.

A mani wheel is a sacred object used in Tibetan Buddhism. Spinning it is said to grant the same virtue as reciting scripture. In this game, you will place various letters on your mani wheel and link together the effects they activate as it spins, gradually building your own engine for generating Virtue.

Combine Letters and Build Your Own Mani Wheel

Letters have a wide variety of effects. Some generate Virtue, some accelerate the wheel, some strengthen adjacent letters, and others generate new letters.

Even a small effect can produce dramatically different results depending on its position, activation order, and connections with the letters above, below, left, and right. Acquire new letters, experiment with their placement, and discover increasingly powerful interactions.

Gather Souls and Combine Front and Back Effects

As you progress, you will unlock Souls that drift around the mani wheel, as well as Letter Fusion, which allows a single letter to carry two separate effects.

Souls produce nothing on their own, but when combined with the right letters, they can generate Virtue, Mercy, or even new letters. Fuse high-rarity letters to create more complex, dual-sided letters whose front and back effects activate in sequence.

Spend Mercy and Open the Path to Reincarnation

Once you have accumulated Mercy, open the Reincarnation Map. Gradually unlock adjacent spaces to permanently strengthen your mani wheel or preserve letters to carry into your next reincarnation.

Each reincarnation expands your options, allowing you to experiment with new combinations and entirely different paths of progression.

Key Features

  • An incremental game supporting both manual control and automatic spinning

  • A wide variety of letter combinations whose effects change based on placement and activation order

  • Six rarity tiers and a letter collection catalog

  • Mid- and late-game systems featuring Souls, Letter Fusion, and dual-sided letters

  • A Reincarnation Map with permanent upgrades unlocked using Mercy

  • A one-lap log that lets you inspect exactly how your setup works

  • Offline progression

  • Available in Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, French, and German

Spin the mani wheel, discover the interactions between its letters, and reincarnate again and again as you find your own path to enlightenment.

About this job

Behind every ATM, there is a hardworking employee. You'll interact with customers and understand their requirements through various instructions.

A business full of endless challenges

Whether it's a simple exchange or a complex transfer, completing tasks will unlock more content step by step.

Transparent career progression

Earn rewards by completing quests and unlock upgrades that help you get things done.

Maintain the work-life balance

Don't forget to enjoy your personal life after work—manage your diet, body shape, and charm.

Your closest companion

Adopt a cat from the Cat Shelter—there might be a little surprise.

Try your luck

Treat yourself to pachinko when you're not working.

Mapping Creator: Draw history the way YOU always wanted!

In Mapping Creator, you are unconstrained by the complex mechanics of other grand strategy games. The world is truly yours to paint, the wars are yours to recreate in detail, and history is what you make of it.

Paint the map the way you want!

Use a wide variety of tools to customise the colours, shapes, names and flags of countries, and make their borders pixel perfect with a brush.

Recreate conflicts in detail!

Click, rotate and drag units on the map to make them advance, form a front line and fight other nations. The location, size and outcome of each engagement is up to you!

Assemble it all for a glorious final timelapse!

Automatically record your gameplay to compile it into a video with no need for additional software.

If you’ve always wanted to decide history down to the smallest details, show how your dream conflict idea would go, and display the final product quickly and easily, this is the game for you!

Every coin you earn, you can see happen.

No abstract ticking number. A marble rolls, hits a peg, chimes — and a coin pops out. That's the whole game, and it's the whole difference. Buy an upgrade and the mill physically rebuilds itself: a new marble rolls in, a new ring bolts on, a bumper lights up. The numbers are a by-product of the machine.

THIS GAME ENDS. ON PURPOSE.

  • ~3 hours to the finale — a real ending, with credits.

  • 100% of the achievements are reachable in that time. No grind wall, no season pass.

  • No dark patterns. No microtransactions. No "wait 4 hours or pay". No ads. Ever.

Then, if you want to stay: an endless sandbox with everything unlocked.

The mill is an instrument

Every hit is pitch-quantized to a pentatonic scale, so a thousand random collisions come out as a chime melody instead of noise. Each era raises the root a fifth — copper C, silver G, gold D, diamond A — so you can hear your progress with your eyes closed. Copper is a muted wooden tock; diamond is glass.

At full tilt the mill fires around 1,900 collisions a second. It doesn't get louder — it gets denser.

Build it out, melt it down

  • Rings bolt on one by one — the machine grows outward like a mandala, up to six rings.

  • Five bumper types: peg, bell, mint (coin geyser), amplifier, prism.

  • Melt the mill down to keep permanent ingots, then rebuild faster in a new material — copper, silver, gold, diamond.

  • Every melt deals you three perk cards and you keep one for the run. A reroll costs an ingot.

  • A rare golden marble rolls through. Click it in time for a bonus. Miss it and you lose nothing.

ASMR mode

One key hides the whole interface. No numbers, no shop, no events — just the machine and the chimes.

Good to know

  • There is no offline income. The mill runs while you're watching it — this is a game you sit with, not a tab you check.

  • It's short by design: ~3 hours to 100%, and then a sandbox to play in.

  • Runs on integrated graphics. It's meant for a laptop on a quiet evening.

Your Mom, The Antagonist

Most of us are told that we only get one mother and one father, but some of us have a different experience.  Play as Derek, a severely neglected and mistreated young man.  You're getting ready to finish off the night when you hear an announcement that it's time for bed, only this announcement comes in the form of anger, hostility and vitriol.

Where are you?  What happened?

After a brief encounter with Mom, you are in somewhat familiar territory, but something is definitely wrong.  Everything is dark, and you definitely aren't in your room anymore.

A Video Game... Inside of an Urban Space... Inside of a Video Game.

Once you realize where you are, it's up to you to beat the game and make it out.  Solve puzzles, follow sequences, listen to the clues, and (hopefully) escape to get back to your normal life...  If that's even where you want to go.  Explore three unique levels, dozens of interactable objects, and a story that is based on truth.

Experience a Unique Perspective - My Perspective

This is my game, and my story.  Based on personal, real experiences.  Some people write books, others BLOG, I made my story into a game, just to be able to tell it in 3D.

Additional Note From The Dev

I wanted to tell my story in a unique way, and this is my very first game.  I have had a desire to create my own game since the SC1 custom map making days, so I took the time and taught myself how to do it.  It's not perfect, but I absolutely loved doing it and plan on continuing to build my skills and create a much more elaborate game in the future as well.  Marbled Memories is unique in the aspect that it can take anywhere from thirty minutes up to two hours to complete and find everything that it has to offer.  Feedback is appreciated.

Marco Polo Shotgun is a casually competitive, chaotic four-player arena shooter where everyone is equipped with the latest and greatest in personal protection: a bulletproof bucket placed on their head. Arm yourself with your trusty double-barrel, embrace your severely restricted visibility, consider your life choices, and try to figure out where the hell everyone else is.

Based on the classic swimming pool game, play as a variety of characters as you stumble around the map trying to find each other. Call out “Marco” to ping your enemies, but reveal your own position. Or stay quiet, listen for footsteps, gunfire, and other environmental cues to hunt down your opponents.

Features:

  • Fast paced, four player arena mayhem

  • Four perspectives to undermine the entire purpose of the game

  • Varied cast of characters to shoot at

  • Over twenty powerups to cause chaos

  • Customisable buckets to express your unique personality

  • Physics based weapons to yeet oneself out the map

  • Advanced bucket physics

  • Fully animated legs

  • Ned Kelly

Run a cozy flower shop in medieval Paris
Maria IV: A Cozy Botanical Sim is a relaxing flower shop simulator and life sim set in late 15th-century Paris, France. As a young florist, you inherit a small flower shop on the Pont Notre-Dame bridge. Grow flowers and plants, run your shop, decorate your home and workspace, and shape the little world your grandmother left you with your own hands.

Grow flowers with real gardening principles
The Guide Book passed down from your grandmother keeps track of every flower you grow, and growing every flower in the book is one of the main goals of the game. Each plant's needs for water, light and care follow real gardening and botany principles, so what you learn in this botanical sim may also help you grow flowers and plants in real life and in your own garden.

Manage, expand and decorate your shop
At its heart, Maria IV is a shop simulator: sell your flowers, manage your stock and income, expand your florist shop and hire employees. Personalize your home and workspace with a wide range of decorations; decorating and organizing your cozy shop is part of the fun, until your little plant shop on the bridge becomes one of the best-known flower shops in Paris.

A historical, atmospheric journey
Explore the atmosphere of historical, late medieval France to Renaissance-inspired music, and uncover the traces of a family legacy passed down through generations.

Features
• A cozy flower shop simulator and life sim in medieval Paris
• Grow flowers and plants with realistic water, light and care needs
• Complete your grandmother's botanical Guide Book
• Shop management: expand your florist shop, hire employees and grow your business
• Decorating: personalize your home and shop
• Relaxing first-person gameplay with Renaissance-inspired music

We hope you enjoy the game.

Mark My Spell is a spellcasting action roguelite about drawing glyphs, typing spells, and building ridiculous synergies to survive a ghost horde.

DRAW A GLYPH. CAST A SPELL.

The ghosts do not care how you cast.

They care very much when a tornado does.

GOLD GOLD GOLD

A wise man once said it. We listened.

Open chests. Find gear. Get stronger. Occasionally accept an item with a downside so alarming it has to be good. Right?

MAKE IT WEIRD.

Pick spells. Add gear. Find the combinations nobody should have approved.

DIE. LEARN. COME BACK STRONGER.

Death is inconvenient. It is not unproductive.

Bring Arcane Ink back from each run. Spend it in a permanent talent tree for new spells, sharper tricks, and a slightly unfair head start next time.

Market Manager Simulator is a detailed and immersive business simulation game where you build and grow your own supermarket from scratch. Starting with a small shop, it’s entirely up to you to stock shelves, set prices, satisfy customers, and expand your business.

In the game, you order products to supply your store, unload them from trucks, and place them on shelves. Shelf organization and product variety directly affect customer behavior. With the right pricing strategies, you can increase your profits and experience competitive market management.

Customers come to your store, pick products from the shelves, and head to the checkout. At the register, you need to scan items one by one and process payments. Managing both cash and card payments quickly and accurately is crucial for customer satisfaction.

Managing your market doesn’t stop there. With the warehouse system, you can stock products and keep your inventory under control. Additionally, the online shopping system allows customers to place orders through a website. You can prepare these orders and personally deliver them to customers across the city to earn extra income.

With the money you earn, you can expand your market and warehouse, and customize areas such as walls, floors, and ceilings to reflect your own style. As your workload increases, you can hire employees such as cashiers, cleaners, and couriers to make your business more efficient.

The game also features an equipment upgrade system. You can upgrade your trucks and carts to complete tasks faster and more efficiently. However, don’t forget to balance expenses such as rent and bills.

In addition, some customers carry rare gold bags. By collecting these, you can use a tablet-based spin wheel system and win extra money rewards depending on your luck.

With its detailed mechanics, freedom of gameplay, and realistic market management experience, Market Manager Simulator invites you to become the boss of your own business.

Immerse yourself in an unsettling psychological horror experience set on a solitary Japanese street during the night shift. Among neon lights, silent cafés, and 24-hour convenience stores, something is not right… and little by little, you will begin to notice it.

In Market Moe, you work the night shift as a warehouse supervisor for several convenience stores. What begins as a quiet routine soon turns into a slow, disturbing nightmare. Paranormal events, impossible behavior, and the haunting presence of the woman in the black dress will begin to distort your perception of reality.



Features

  • Immersive psychological horror
    An experience focused on tension, discomfort, and gradual fear.

  • Detailed Japanese setting
    Explore a street with cafés, vending machines, and a fully interactive convenience store.

  • Environmental storytelling
    The story is revealed through small details, events, and changes in the environment.

  • First-person experience
    Designed for maximum immersion.

  • Atmospheric audio
    Subtle sounds that generate paranoia and constant tension.

In Market Panic, every run is a ten-year market cycle and every quarter is a new test of nerve. Run an investment firm across stocks, bonds, cash, hedges, credit, private equity and crypto. Queue your moves, read the closing plan, and ring the bell - or don't, and explain to the committee why not.

Read what is inside the book

A sleeve is not one number. Open it and there are six companies inside, each with its own weight, ticker, candlestick chart and return - fourteen sleeves, eighty-four companies. One holding is usually carrying the fund and one is usually wrecking it, and you can tell which. Every chart opens on three years of tape from before your mandate began, so you are never reading a market that started the day you did.

The market is never completely safe

Bank runs, inflation shocks, speculative bubbles, liquidity freezes, scandals and twenty-seven named crises can expose a book that looked sensible a quarter ago. Movement arrives in clusters: quiet stretches, then a handful of quarters that do most of the damage. Nothing warns you twice, and nothing on the screen is there to tell you what happens next.

Clients who can leave

Fourteen institutions, nine dealt into each run, five of them on your books from the first morning - a pension fund with retirees to pay, a family office that wants spectacular returns and hates playing safe, a reinsurer that pays out when the storms land, a union that will not subsidise anyone's speculation. Each has a promise the market can break, a board review on its calendar, and somewhere else to take its money.

The rivals across the road

Four rival houses share Kingsgate Tower, across the road from your building, drawn each run from eight. They have real portfolios, their own ideas about the next trade, and their own ideas about which of your accounts they would rather hold. Walk over. Ride up to a rival's floor and read the room: the whiteboard, the principal, who is at their desk and who is not. Then poach a trader, plant a story, make a bet with them, call a truce - or buy one of them outright.

Down the road, the City Exchange

The trading floor under the gallery, the board over it, the brokers' bar and the bell. Take a seat, ring it, list your own firm - and watch the crowd on the floor react to the market you have been trading all along.

And you can stand up

Step back from the terminal and it turns out to be a monitor on a desk, on a floor of a building, in a city. The office is drawn from the state of your run: a lamp on a desk for each client, colleagues who sit differently depending on how it is going, the committee member who has lost the most faith waiting on the floor when you get up. Take the lift down, walk out onto the street, buy the paper - the city's papers report your run as it happens.

Ten years, on film

When the run ends, however it ends, the game cuts the film of your ten years: the quarters that mattered, the calls that made it and the ones that broke it. Watch it, replay it, save it.

Finance as drama, not homework

You do not need to know finance. On your first run a colleague at the next desk explains each control the first time you rest on it, in a sentence. Research rumors, negotiate mandates, document risk exceptions, test crisis scenarios, protect liquidity, or take the aggressive line. The aim is not merely to finish with the best return. It is to build the institution that survives long enough to tell its investors why it did what it did.

Features

  • Turn-based roguelite runs across a full ten-year market cycle: forty quarters, each closed by a bell you choose to ring

  • Six firms, five of them earned by how you play, each with its own book, temperament and way of losing

  • Build across stocks, bonds, cash, hedges, credit, private equity and crypto - fourteen sleeves, eighty-four companies, each with three years of tape from before your mandate began

  • Twenty-seven named crises, from bank runs to liquidity freezes, and hundreds of smaller shocks that arrive in clusters

  • Fourteen institutional clients, nine dealt into each run, five of them on your books from the first morning - every one with a promise the market can break

  • Four rival houses each run, drawn from eight, with real portfolios, grudges, truces and designs on your accounts

  • Walk the city: your office floor, the lift, the street, the rivals' tower across the road and the City Exchange down it

  • Read a rival's floor - its whiteboard, its principal, its staff - then poach, plant a story, place a bet, or buy the house outright

  • Take a seat on the City Exchange, ring its bell, and list your own firm

  • An investment committee that drafts standing policy, reads every close and remembers what you did not answer

  • The city's papers report your run, and at the end of it the game cuts the film of your ten years

  • On your first run, a colleague at the next desk explains each control the first time you rest on it - no finance knowledge required

  • Forty achievements, most of them hard and some of them rude

  • Adaptive music, authored market audio and a building that sounds like one

  • Nine languages: the market writing, the briefs and the endings, not only the menus

Nine languages

Playable in English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German, French, Turkish, Japanese, Russian and Simplified Chinese - the market writing, the briefs and the endings included, not only the menus.

Explore. Trade. Fish. Whale. Colonize. Fight. Pillage. Survive. You are a sea captain in the year 1522, and the whole world is yours to discover in this roguelike sandbox historical sailing simulator.

The world of Marque & Reprisal is a fully realized, 655,362-tile, 331-city map of the entire Earth, complete with accurate geography, navigable rivers and lakes, mountains, a detailed weather simulation, and many ancient and natural wonders to discover.

The cities and villages of the world buy and sell different goods at different prices, with supply and demand for goods and specie reacting dynamically to the actions of the player and the hundreds of NPC ships plying the trade routes in search of riches.

Fish for many different species of fish! Upgrade your ship and your net to catch more fish, and sell them in the best markets to earn profits.

The ocean contains great and mysterious beasts! There are multiple different whale species in the game, with ecologically accurate ranges and behaviours. Whales breed and have babies, and you can often see a whale calf following its mother through the ocean. Kill a whale with your harpoon and collect its valuable blubber to sell!

Perhaps on your journey you will meet colonists seeking passage to the New World. Help them and you may found new cities together.

Do battle with pirates and hostile nations! Or become a pirate yourself and set out in search of rich merchant ships to seize.

With a large enough warship, you can bombard a hostile city to silence its shore batteries, then land marines to capture the port!

When it's time to take a port, your crew leaps off the ship and engages in auto-battler combat with the port's garrison.


If you die in Marque & Reprisal, there's no going back. You need to start a new voyage with a new captain. Death comes in many forms, from hunger and thirst to stormy seas and pirate attacks.

20XX.

Japan is facing a severe decline in its birthrate, and the government has introduced one new policy after another to combat the crisis.

Unmarried people aged 30 and over are now subject to a hefty “Singles Tax.”

Companies have even begun avoiding unmarried employees in their thirties—

And on the day you turn 30, your company suddenly gives you an ultimatum:

“Get married within one month—or you’re fired.”

Determined to save your job, you head to a matchmaking agency.

But getting married isn’t going to be that easy.

To meet the requirements of your potential partners, you’ll need to change your stats:

Intelligence, Age, Cleanliness, Height, and Income.

Solve puzzles, use items, and find all kinds of ways to alter your stats.

Sometimes, the solution may be something you never expected…

Can you manage to get married

within just one month?

  • A puzzle game themed around matchmaking and marriage.

  • Hints are available.

  • The difficulty level is middle〜high.

  • Use your stats and items to figure out how to get married.

  • A casual puzzle game focused on clever ideas and creative solutions.

[Estimated Playtime]

120–180 minutes

[Streaming & Video Content]

You are welcome to stream, record, and upload gameplay videos of this game.

Monetized videos and streams are also allowed.

[Sound Effects]

  • Sound Effect Lab

Welcome to the Chaos

You're not the chosen one. Not the hero with a tragic backstory. Not special anything. Just an average wizard who showed up and said "how hard can it be?". And somehow they still picked you for the task.

Battle hordes of enemies and epic bosses in this unique take on a bullet-heaven roguelite where the faster you kill, the stronger you become. Gather relics and choose the abilities that augment your playstyle, creating ridiculously powerful synergies. Transcend the definition of bullet heaven! Cover the whole zone with auras that kill enemies as they spawn! Summon a flurry of weapons to do your bidding!

Grow and grow and grow in power till you break the world itself!

Combat - Go strong, go quick

The combat in Master of Chaos revolves around two main mechanics: combos and chainable counterattacks.

Unlike the build-conditional mechanics found in several bullet-heaven games, the combo in Master of Chaos is always active, granting you more bonuses the bigger the combo grows. How high can you get? There have been rumors of combos reaching tens of thousands...

Supporting the combo mechanic is the ability to counterattack, protecting yourself from damage while damaging the enemy in turn. Every time you successfully counterattack, you can repeat the action immediately! Nothing frustrates the monsters quite as much as flashing through their ranks, leaving a trail of the dead in your wake while you pass unscathed.

Upgrades - Strategy and skill triumph over luck

Master of Chaos takes the synergy between abilities to a whole new level. Everything affects everything, and the tiniest change could reshape the whole build. Add an ability, and one projectile becomes three. Add another, and they're spinning in wild spirals. Add a third, that by itself wouldn't have made a difference, and you have a solid field of projectiles obliterating everything in their path.

Abilities are gained by acquiring relics, whether from loot boxes via quests, minibosses or regular enemies, or by crafting or buying from shops. The loot boxes might at first glance appear random, but as with everything in the game, skill pays off. It is up to you when the reels of relic choices stop spinning. Yours to decide which relic to aim for, or whether you forego the small rewards and pursue the jackpot for a big payout.

Unleash Chaos on the Battlefield

As an alternative way to win, Master of Chaos features a unique mechanic for the truly dedicated gamebreaker. Stack enough upgrades, chain enough kills, push your combo high enough and the game itself will start to buckle under the weight of your power. Shadows disappear, draw distances shrink, resolution crumbles, until there is nothing left. At that point, the game itself has no choice but to admit defeat and hand you the victory.

Do you have what it takes to break the game and claim the title of the true Master of Chaos?

Match & Drop: Pachinko Rush

Are you ready for the ultimate fusion of match-3 puzzles and physics-based Pachinko excitement? Match colorful tiles, launch bouncy balls across bouncy pegs into multiplier slots, and hit massive score combos!

KEY FEATURES

  • Unique Hybrid Gameplay: A satisfying blend of classic match-3 puzzle mechanics and physics-driven Pachinko action.

  • Destructive Power-Ups: Create 4 and 5-matches to unleash Explosive Bombs, chain Lightning, and the Cosmic Black Hole that wipes out all tiles of the same color!

  • Permanent Upgrade System: Spend your earned EXP to permanently upgrade extra balls per match, lucky slot multipliers, and critical ball drop rates.

  • Risk & Reward (Penalty Slot): Aim carefully! While most slots multiply your score and grant EXP, the Red Penalty Slot deducts points. Every drop is a strategic decision!

  • Global Leaderboards: Your score and level are synchronized in real-time with Steam Global Leaderboards. Climb to the top and compete worldwide!

  • Wide Language Support: Fully localized in 27 languages.

HOW TO PLAY

  • Match: Swap and match 3 or more tiles of the same color to clear them.

  • Drop: Each cleared tile spawns bouncy balls that ricochet down through the peg field.

  • Hit Multipliers: Guide balls into high-multiplier slots (x5, x10, Lucky 2x) to boost your score!

  • Upgrade: Level up, earn EXP, buy permanent upgrades, and crush your high scores!

The card you play changes what the next mercenary can do. Match & Ruin is a roguelike card battler built around three mercenaries and the familiar ranks and suits of playing cards.

Set up the next move


Play a card that matches the rank or suit of the card on the table. The card you play becomes the top card for the next mercenary to match. Check the next mercenary's hand and choose a card that sets them up to attack, defend, or use the skill your party needs.

Attack, defend, or use a skill


Each mercenary uses the same hand for attacks, defense, and skills. Read the enemy's next attack and plan who will strike, who needs to guard, and which skill can turn the fight.

Overload their hand


Stack draw penalties to push the enemy over its hand limit. You can win even while it still has HP.

Shape your deck


Your mercenaries and the enemy draw from the same deck. Duplicate useful cards, remove unwanted cards, and change their suits. Your changes affect both sides. Collect relics and trinkets, improve your mercenaries' skills, and use consumables to rescue a bad hand as you travel through fallen kingdoms.

Two games, one idea.

Matchinko is a match-3 puzzle that feeds a physics-driven pachinko payout, wrapped in a roguelite of tiles, ball loadouts, and a fate-navigated map.

First you build the board by matching.

Then you break it — raining your loadout of balls through the pegs you just made for a score that snowballs out of control.

You are the lamp keeper, travelling town to town. Charge the crystals, string the lights across the houses, and dispel the darkness that caps each town. Clear it, and the town shines.

[h2]Build, then break[/h2]

  • A single persistent board carries through your whole run — you compound it, you never restart it.

  • Spend your moves matching 3+ crystals: merged crystals rise a level and score exponentially more.

  • Then drop your ball loadout. Every peg and tile it touches pays out. A smart merge now is a jackpot later.

[h2]No two runs play alike[/h2]

Buy from the townsfolk between matches and your whole playstyle changes:

  • 30 fairies — 15 common, 10 rare, and 5 event-only legendaries — that orbit your board and bend the rules: magnets, midas coins, phoenix revivals, chain-lightning, and more.

  • 36 tiles — special pegs from splash detonations to greed engines, including 5 legendary "grow cards" that start small and snowball the longer you keep them.

  • 30 balls — a loadout deck across common, rare, and legendary tiers, plus 3 editions (Gilded, Radiant, Prismatic) that add a shine on top of the ball's own trick.

  • 11 events — risk/reward encounters on the map: wishing wells, enchanters, cursed bargains, ember altars. Push your luck or play it safe.

A climb to the boss

Every run is a 12-level branching climb. Each level is its own procedural winter town; a boss caps every third one. Bosses are known in advance, so your shopping has direction — buy to beat the rule you can see coming. Light all four towns and topple the final boss to win the run.

One miss away

Miss a level's target and the run ends immediately — back to a fresh board. Roguelite stakes, not casual comfort. Every ball counts.

Cozy on the outside

Hand-drawn snow-capped villages, chimney smoke, a lamplighter tending the post, drifting snow, and a garland of lights that fills in as you clear each town. The reward isn't just a coin count — it's a dark town coming to light.
